deep.reconstruction:
Grothendieck sets up a combinatorial framework for categories of 'models' (shapes). The previous page counts sub-objects of D_n as 1 + n·2 + C(n,2)·2^2 + … + 2^n = 3^n, which is the number of faces of the n-cube. So the guiding example is cubes with face inclusions. The previous page also states that presheaves on the 'basic objects' D_n compute (Gr-stacks), so colimits are computed componentwise.

On this page M is any category satisfying two conditions:
(i) every arrow is a monomorphism;
(ii) every endomorphism of an object is the identity.
In modern terms M is a one-way (EI-type) category with trivial automorphism groups and only monos; posets viewed as categories are the given example.

For each object D, let D̃ be the poset of sub-objects of D under inclusion, with D identified with its top element. For objects D', D the map Hom(D', D) → D̃, u ↦ u(D') is injective: if two arrows u, v give the same sub-object, they differ by an automorphism of D', which is the identity by (ii). Its image is the set Φ_{D'}(D) of sub-objects of D that are M-isomorphic to D'.

Let N be the set of isomorphism classes of objects, preordered by existence of arrows. It is in fact a partial order: if D → D' → D, the composite is the identity by (ii), and a mono that is split is an iso. Each class n has a representative D_n determined up to unique isomorphism (by (ii)). Hence the posets D̃_n are well defined up to unique isomorphism, giving a family (D̃_n)_{n∈N} of posets indexed by the poset N.

The next page continues the programme:
- a 'type' map T_n : D̃_n → N, strictly increasing, with image N_{≤n};
- the fibres T_n^{-1}(n') are in bijection with Hom(D_{n'}, D_n);
- injective maps ρ_{n,n'} from these fibres into Hom(D̃_{n'}, D̃_n).

The evident aim is to recover M, and presheaves on M, from the purely order-theoretic data (N, D̃_n, T_n, ρ). This would describe cell-shape categories such as cubes or simplices with face maps by their face posets.
errors: Only (ii), plus the fact that arrows define sub-objects (which uses (i)), is needed for injectivity; citing both is harmless.
Implicit size assumption: D̃ and N are sets only if M is (essentially) small and well-powered; not stated.
Minor: the text says 'élément de M' where 'objet' is meant.

ideas.what: Categories in which all arrows are mono and all endomorphisms are identities; N = poset of iso classes
ideas.modern_name: direct / one-way categories (EI categories with trivial automorphisms), skeleta as 'gaunt' shape categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Reedy (1974) for Reedy/direct categories; folklore for EI categories (tom Dieck, Lück)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related remarks on test categories and shapes in Pursuing Stacks; not this formulation as far as known

ideas.what: Embedding Hom(D',D) into the sub-object poset of D, image = sub-objects isomorphic to D'
ideas.modern_name: faces of a cell as sub-objects; face poset of a regular cell / semi-cubical or semi-simplicial shape

ideas.what: Encoding the category by the family of face posets (D̃_n) indexed by N, with type maps (continued on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: face-poset description of cell categories; related to regular CW complexes / Reedy-category combinatorics
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (cf. combinatorial topology of regular cell complexes)

missed.claim: A programme to reconstruct a category of 'models' (e.g. semi-cubes with 3^n faces) and its presheaf category from the order-theoretic data of face posets with type maps, apparently in service of describing (Gr-)stacks combinatorially. The thread is set up but not completed on these pages. Comparable modern material exists (direct/Reedy categories, face posets), so novelty is limited.
missed.quote: On a donc une famille (Ñ_n)_{n ∈ N} d'ens ordonnés, indexés par l'ensemble ordonné N.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mostly of historical interest: it documents Grothendieck working with direct/semi-cubical shape categories in a stack context. It is unlikely to contain unknown mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard elementary facts about categories with only monos and trivial endomorphisms (direct/EI categories), set up as a foundation. There is nothing beyond folklore on this page itself.
transcription_corrections: The symbol written for the set of iso classes is a bold/double-struck N (𝐍), denoting the poset of iso classes, not the natural numbers. The next-page transcription's ℕ should be read as this same poset N.
'D̃_n = Ñ_n [?]' in the image looks like D̃_n = 𝐃̃_n (a decorated D), i.e. a notation for the poset attached to class n rather than Ñ.
In the margin, 'M-' is inserted before 'isomorphes'; and 'Il est en fait ordonné, grâce à (ii)' is an insertion above the line, as transcribed.
